links.outcome: Reproducibility of delirium identification across repeated independent and consecutive sessions
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% of cases in both independent sessions and 90% in consecutive-session run; agreement between independent sessions κ=0.76, but low agreement involving consecutive run, suggesting contextual priming.
links.quote: Agreement between independent ChatGPT-4o sessions was substantial (κ=0.76), while agreement involving the consecutive-session run was low, suggesting contextual priming.

links.outcome: Delirium identification of ChatGPT-4o versus comparator model DeepSeek-V2 on same vignettes
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% (independent sessions) and 90% (consecutive run) of cases, whereas DeepSeek-V2 identified 50%.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% of cases in both independent sessions and 90% in the consecutive-session run, whereas DeepSeek-V2 identified 50%.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic performance and consistency of ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V2 on clinical vignettes of delirium, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
